title: Portable JSON admission
responsibility: Checks whether values can retain their meaning across supported JSON runtimes within the nesting bound.

inputs.name: portableJson.value
inputs.description: The value to inspect: a finite number, a well-formed string, a boolean, null, an array, or an object whose prototype is Object.prototype or null. For objects, only own enumerable string-keyed fields are checked and undefined fields are skipped; undefined outside object fields, NaN or infinite numbers, strings or keys with lone surrogates, functions, symbols, bigints, non-array objects with another prototype and nesting beyond 64 levels make the result false.
inputs.unknownReason: This guard tests arbitrary input recursively for compatibility with the portable JSON runtime.

inputs.name: portableJson.level
inputs.description: Number of arrays or objects already enclosing the value; it defaults to 0 and each container entered adds one. Objects and arrays are refused once it reaches maxJsonDepth (64), and it is not validated, so a negative start allows more than 64 levels.

outputs.name: maxJsonDepth
outputs.description: The deepest array or object nesting that portableJson accepts, exported as a const holding 64. A nested array or object is refused once its level reaches this value, so at most 64 nested containers pass.

outputs.name: portableJson
outputs.description: True when every number is finite, every string and every object key with a defined value is well-formed, every non-array object has a plain or null prototype, and nesting stays within maxJsonDepth; false otherwise. The input is checked in place and is never cloned or serialized.

outputs.name: notPortable
outputs.description: Shared failure response created once by runtimeFailure('invalid-json', 'request is not valid JSON') and exported as a single object that is not frozen. portableJson never returns or throws it; it only returns true or false, so callers decide whether to use it.
